To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the noncatalytic R-domains of AlgE4 (and by implication AlgE1–3) bind alginate, and the R-domains of the AlgE6 (and by implication the other epimerases) do not bind alginate.

the noncatalytic subunit of AlgE6 has an alginate binding groove that is different from that of AlgE4 despite highly similar structures and that the noncata-lytic domains of AlgE6 influence the product specificity.

we have solved the structure of the three R-modules from the alginate epimerase AlgE6 and have shown that they have a different alginate binding ability compared with the R-module from the epimerase AlgA4.

the structural and functional characterization of the R-modules from Alginate C- 5 epimerases AlgE6 and the R-modules from the closely related epimerase AlgE4
the structural and functional characterization of the R-modules and their role in the alginate C-5 epimerses from A. vinelandii.
the structure and function of the R-modules from Alginate C- 5 Epimerases and their influence on the product specificity of Alginate Epimerases.

AlgE4R binds to both M and MG oligomers, whereas the individual R-modules of Alg6 bind to neither.

the R-module from AlgE6 does not have a direct alginate binding ability, but the R-modules from both enzymes have a regulatory effect on the A-modules, which in turn influences the product specificity.
the noncatalytic R-modules of AlgA epimerases influence both the binding affinity and the specificity of the catalytically active A-modules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the R-modules of alginate epimerase AlgE4 and 6 have a distinct alginate binding ability and influence the product specificity in a modular way.

the individual R-modules of AlgA4 and AlgE64 have a different alginate binding ability despite a high degree of sequence similarity, and the R-modules of the two enzymes are functionally exchangeable.

the R-modules from Alginate epimerase AlgE4 and the R1R2R1 combination of AlgE6 have a strong alginate binding ability, whereas the R-modules from the R1R3R2 combination of AlgE4 are not able to interact with alginate polymers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the R-modules in the AlgE4 family have a strong alginate binding capacity, which may be important for the product specificity and processivity of the epimerases.
R-modules from different epimerases have distinct alginate-binding abilities despite having very similar structures, which can be exploited for the design of novel epimerases.
